Sentence (English): I wanted to love this thing so bad.
Comments (English): [ Don't love it ] || ---------------- || I wanted to love this thing so bad. A few issues: 1. I love the idea of the drawers but I can't seem to fit my dishes in in a way that makes sense. 2. Even with rinse aid, my top drawer always leaves powdery residue. it's not because of the pod because it doesn't do it on the bottom drawer. See pictures. 3. The plastic cake plate at the bottom is so cheap and cheesy. 4. I have no idea if the cycle is finished or not. There's not a lights or anything to let me know that the dishwasher is through. If you are not standing in the kitchen when the charm goes off, you have no idea it's done with the cycle. 5. Neither the physical buttons on the dishwasher, nor the explanation in the user manual, give a good explanation of the cycles, and how to use things. I still cannot figure out how to do some of the things. 6. The top drawer does not dry for anything. There's always a big puddle of water in the bottom of the drawer and the dishes are always dripping wet after the cycle is done. Not really happy at all with this dishwasher.

I love the idea of the drawers but I can't seem to fit my dishes in in a way that makes sense. 2. Even with rinse aid, my top drawer always leaves powdery residue. it's not because of the pod because it doesn't do it on the bottom drawer. See pictures. 3. The plastic cake plate at the bottom is so cheap and cheesy. 4. I have no idea if the cycle is finished or not. There's not a lights or anything to let me know that the dishwasher is through. If you are not standing in the kitchen when the charm goes off, you have no idea it's done with the cycle. 5. Neither the physical buttons on the dishwasher, nor the explanation in the user manual, give a good explanation of the cycles, and how to use things. I still cannot figure out how to do some of the things. 6. The top drawer does not dry for anything. There's always a big puddle of water in the bottom of the drawer and the dishes are always dripping wet after the cycle is done. Not really happy at all with this dishwasher.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher barely dries the dishes and I still don't know if they are actually drying from the dishwasher feature or if they are just drip-drying.
Comments (English): [ Worst Dishwasher Ever ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher barely dries the dishes and I still don't know if they are actually drying from the dishwasher feature or if they are just drip-drying. The included pictures were taken 20 hours after I started a Normal Wash cycle with High Heat and Extended Dry. You will see that the door and the bottom of the dishwasher are still wet. I had a Kenmore dishwasher prior to this one and it would be bone dry less than two hours after the wash cycle was completed. I really miss that dishwasher and it's only been gone for a little over a week. The three racks in this dishwasher stay wet and the third rack is the worst one. As soon as you pull it open, all of the water drips down on the \"dry\" dishes underneath it. I know that the easy solution is to pull it open last but I shouldn't have to. This is, by far, the worst dishwasher I have ever used. It looks nice, and the racks roll very smoothly on their tracks but those are the only nice things that I can say about this one. Just a word of warning to the customers in New York and New Jersey. If you pay for \"Professional Installation,\" they are going to send a third party to your house that will pull out your old dishwasher and then tell you that you have to pay for a new shutoff valve (even if you don't need one) that will cost you an extra $150 that isn't covered by Best Buy. If you don't pay, they won't install your new dishwasher and they will leave your old one at the curb. This is what they did to me and many others that I discovered after researching their company. If your old dishwasher is hard-wired, they won't install the new one. It's going to cost you an extra $200 for them to install an outlet.

If Bosch updated their interface, I would have given this 5 stars.

Sentence (English): Overall, the dishwasher is a 9 out of 10.
Comments (English): [ Great features - But! ] || ---------------- || Overall, the dishwasher is a 9 out of 10. Top rack is great for small, flat pieces like splatter screens, spatulas, wooden spoons, pizza pans and cooking tongs. Second rack has ample room for rows and rows of drinkware and small bowls. Bottom rack will fit about 10-12 large and 10-12 small plates and tons of room for eating utensils in the utensil tray. Multiple choices for washing cycles with boost feature which I was looking for because I love having completely dry dishes before I store them in the cupboard. However, even after a normal 3 1/2-hour wash cycle with the boost feature and drying agent overnight, I will open the dishwasher to find all cups with water pooled on the top of them and the sides of the drum and door with moisture as if it were a continuously running humidifier. This is annoying, and since I worry about a mold inducing situation occurring, I have to use a dry towel to wipe down the entire cavity of the dishwasher until it is dry. Not my idea of a sufficiently operating appliance! I do love the look and the quietness of the unit and overall, I am satisfied with my purchase. But please, please fix the wetness issue!

The adjustable (up or down) middle rack is perfect as sometimes I have bottles or large glasses (down position) and when there are taller plates or cookware in the bottom, I can move the middle rack up. Most of the time everything comes out clean and shiny, but not always. One problem is the tine placement on the bottom - my square dishes don't sit evenly and sometimes fall onto one another which causes spotty washing. (see picture). Bowls towards the front of the middle rack sometimes come out unwashed too - I suspect from the angle they sometimes end up sitting. I haven't tried different detergents, but do keep the rinse aid full and still my thin wine glasses end up with very small water spots that I have to wipe off. Maybe a different detergent brand would alleviate this? I get a notification in the Smart HQ app when the cycle is complete - I haven't really been able to use the remote start through the app - not as easy as it sounds, need to read up on that more.

Sentence (English): It's so quiet compared to my previous one, that sometimes I don't understand if it's working or not.
Comments (English): [ Very silent! Consume nothing. ] || ---------------- || It's so quiet compared to my previous one, that sometimes I don't understand if it's working or not. Convenient the light on the floor that allows you to understand if he is washing or if he has finished. The fact of being able to connect it to the mobile phone to get remote alerts on the lack of salt or rinse aid and on the time remaining at the end of the cycle is excellent. Really low consumption, for an eco wash I measured between 0.70 and 0.80 kWh. It washes very well and with very little water (nine and a half liters per wash! ). It has protection on the pipe against flooding. To get to these levels, however, he has to do very long washes so the Eco wash lasts four and a half hours. There is also the possibility of reducing the times up to an hour but I have never tried the short wash. The fact that it can be connected directly to the hot water that I produce with a solar thermal panel is excellent. Those who produce hot water with a heat pump will also benefit. When I connected it to my mobile phone, the app hesitated and didn't immediately recognize the dishwasher, so I promptly called the assistance service thinking it was a defect. They answered me immediately, cordially (and competently!) and reassured me, asking me to wait a few seconds. As I spoke to the operator, everything fell into place. Defects:. 1) requires salt in granules, while I use the one in tablets (from a water softener). In this case the salt presence sensor tells me that I have to add it even if it is full. 2) even if prepared, in this model the top basket cannot be raised or lowered to have more space in the basket below. However excellent dishwasher, I would buy it again immediately.

Sentence (English): The good: The dishwasher cleans the dishes and dries with no problem, I use the Cascade premium dishwasher tabs as I always have, they just do a better job than the others I have tried.
Comments (English): [ Kitchen Aid Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The good: The dishwasher cleans the dishes and dries with no problem, I use the Cascade premium dishwasher tabs as I always have, they just do a better job than the others I have tried. I have found leaving the dishes in the dishwasher for 2 hours after the cycle is finished ensures the dishes are completely dry, using jet dry is also a plus for drying the dishes. The dishwasher has great features and does a great job of removing even the most stubborn of food stains and seems to work well with plastics in the upper rack. The dishwasher is quiet and looks great with my kitchen decor and is easy to clean. The racks move smoothly in and out as well as the door opens and closes with ease. The silverware basket is well designed for all types of silverware and is easily removable and is easily adjustable for odd sized items. The concerns: The dishwasher has a plastic frame it sits on and not a steel frame, my first dishwasher arrived with a broken frame after it appears it was dropped on the corner, this was due to a poor shipping frame the dishwasher was shipped on, the issue was not even noticed until the box was completely removed. The pump sits very low due the cavernous size of the interior of the dishwasher, and there is a lot of plastic parts underneath but they appear to be solid. The plastic drain on the side of the dishwasher also has me concerned of its durability, and those that have a tight dishwasher space need to make sure they do have 24 inches of clearance to place this dishwasher in between cabinets it does fit snug with the insulation. The tines in the dishwasher are smaller than my old dishwasher, and it does not have fold down sections to facilitate larger bowl and pans. the second rack is easily adjustable to accommodate taller dishes in the bottom rack, the second rack holds plenty of glasses and bowls, but bowls in center rack lean to left due to the design of the sprayer arm, but it cleans all the dishes in the the rack efficiently. The third rack is good only for small silverware, lids and larger serving silverware, there is not much clearance or adjustment for the rack, the more expensive models have a much nicer and more usable third rack. Final thoughts: The dishwasher does an excellent job of cleaning the dishes, and that is the most important feature of this model, hopefully the construction and reliability will live up to the Kitchen Aid name, only time will tell. I researched dishwashers from every brand and every price range, and this one works and does what its supposed to do very well. I would look at the higher end models and see if those features I mentioned may make a difference, otherwise this dishwasher will clean every dish in your cabinet, all your silverware and glasses if you want it too, it has tons of room. It appears to be a good and effective design, with a few tweaks it could be great, that's what we should expect from a Kitchen Aid appliance!

Comments (English): [ Worst Dishwasher Ever ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher barely dries the dishes and I still don't know if they are actually drying from the dishwasher feature or if they are just drip-drying. I had a Kenmore dishwasher prior to this one and it would be bone dry less than two hours after the wash cycle was completed. I really miss that dishwasher and it's only been gone for a little over a week.The three racks in this dishwasher stay wet and the third rack is the worst one. As soon as you pull it open, all of the water drips down on the "dry" dishes underneath it. I know that the easy solution is to pull it open last but I shouldn't have to. This is, by far, the worst dishwasher I have ever used. It looks nice, and the racks roll very smoothly on their tracks but those are the only nice things that I can say about this one. Just a word of warning to the customers in New York and New Jersey. If you don't pay, they won't install your new dishwasher and they will leave your old one at the curb. This is what they did to me and many others that I discovered after researching their company. Sentence (English): This is our third KitchenAid dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Excellent So Far ] || ---------------- || This is our third KitchenAid dishwasher. I've always loved the third rack and the flexibility KA dishwashers provide. I installed this in January and its performance has been excellent. The new controls and options were fairly intuitive especially since our last dishwasher was KA. The new third rack on top is fantastic and has added even more flexibility when loading a myriad of items. It also seems that the interior is more spacious. Most importantly dishes and utensils come out sparkling clean and dry while the dishwasher is fairly quiet. The fan-enabled Pro Dry system works well even with plastic containers, though you need to let it run its full course to get best results. Even if the complete wash cycle has completed and the "Clean" indicator lights up, the fan will continue to run. If you open the door, the fan will shut off and will not come back on when closed. Most of the large dishes were dry but some plastic lids and glasses were still wet. The PrintShield stainless steel does seems to "resist" fingerprints and other stains. I was constantly wiping down our old dishwasher but I've only wiped off some minor fingerprints once so far. I do wish KA gave the option to install the previous arched handle of the older KA line. Our other KA appliances still have the arched handles and I think they look more elegant than the more industrial look of the current handles. Overall, its a nice upgrade from our last KA dishwasher. It's quiet, more flexible and most importantly gets our dishes clean and dry. Hoping to get at least 8 years out of it. Most plumbers will tell you that dishwashers these days only last 6-10 years on average and that's was our experience with our last KA dishwasher lasting 8 years. Crossing fingers that we'll get more out of this one.

Sentence (English): I really like this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Very Quiet ] || ---------------- || I really like this dishwasher. It cleans all the dishes and glassware and leaves no residue. It is super quiet and you can't hear it unless you really listen. I did have a minor issue with it when it was delivered. The bar holding the third rake had a piece that was broken off. We called Lowes and they arranged to have a local repairman come to fix the part the next day. There was one other issue which was not found until my husband was hooking it all up and that was that the frame underneath the dishwasher was bent. This most likely occurred by dropping the dishwasher while in the box as there was no sign of damage on the outside of the dishwasher itself. You could only see the frame was bent when we had it lying on its side. My husband was able to bend it back enough for us to get it installed. We probably should have returned it but we had it all apart at that point and didn't think they would accept it back. The dishwasher itself works great it was how it was handled that was not good.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher in May of 2021.
Comments (English): [ Worked well when it worked ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher in May of 2021. The first one had an electrical issue within the first two months of ownership. We had the warranty repair people out. They ordered parts, which were then backordered. Then we had to wait 21 days. After that, they determined that the parts were unavailable and they replaced the dishwasher. One month later, it was working just fine. To be safe, we purchased an extended warranty with the replacement unit. The dishwasher worked pretty well until September of 2022 (~1 year 2 mos), when the sensor in the motor unit failed. The dishwasher overfilled and dumped water out and then wouldn't work anymore. We contacted the warranty company who sent out a repair person. The repair person replaced the entire motor unit using OEM parts, so after two visits and about a month, we had our dishwasher back. It was a lot louder, though. We reported that to the repair people and they said that it was normal. But it went from near silent to really quite loud. So then we used it for a while. All along there was a wet mold smell coming from under the kitchen sink. We use cloth rags that are stored in a bucket under the sink after use, so we thought the odor was those. Then after Christmas, we realized that the floor was starting to heave. I took the front plate off of the dishwasher, and lo and behold the new pump was dripping on the floor, quite a lot, too. I removed the dishwasher at that point and realized that is had been leaking apparently since the pump was replaced and had gotten under the flooring and underlayment. I borrowed a moisture meter from work and determined that it had affected 25-35% of my kitchen floor. I contacted the warranty company on January 4, 2023, who promptly dispatched repair people. They indicated that the new pump was faulty and was leaking. They said that they'd order the new part and would get back to us. I am writing this review on March 7, 2023, and my dishwasher is still broken. I was notified on Friday that the part was backordered and a 21 day cycle was started then. So maybe I'll have a functional dishwasher by the end of March. Perhaps some of the time delay is due to a poor repair company, but the unit has still broken 3 times now, which is not what I'd expect at this cost point. We have had this since May of 2021, so about 22 months. For 17 of those months, it was a good dishwasher; However, it has been out of order for the other 5 months, so about 20% of the time we've owned it. Just to be clear, our last dishwasher was an old Fisher Paykel that we bought used for 200 dollars that we used for 5 years and gave away working. It never broke once.

The repair person replaced the entire motor unit using OEM parts, so after two visits and about a month, we had our dishwasher back. It was a lot louder, though. We reported that to the repair people and they said that it was normal. But it went from near silent to really quite loud. So then we used it for a while. All along there was a wet mold smell coming from under the kitchen sink. We use cloth rags that are stored in a bucket under the sink after use, so we thought the odor was those. Then after Christmas, we realized that the floor was starting to heave. I took the front plate off of the dishwasher, and lo and behold the new pump was dripping on the floor, quite a lot, too. I removed the dishwasher at that point and realized that is had been leaking apparently since the pump was replaced and had gotten under the flooring and underlayment. I borrowed a moisture meter from work and determined that it had affected 25-35% of my kitchen floor. I contacted the warranty company on January 4, 2023, who promptly dispatched repair people. They indicated that the new pump was faulty and was leaking. They said that they'd order the new part and would get back to us. I am writing this review on March 7, 2023, and my dishwasher is still broken. I was notified on Friday that the part was backordered and a 21 day cycle was started then. So maybe I'll have a functional dishwasher by the end of March. Just to be clear, our last dishwasher was an old Fisher Paykel that we bought used for 200 dollars that we used for 5 years and gave away working. It never broke once.

Even though a 50 cent piece is going to end up costing me 25 dollars, it might preserve my sanity today. Still to experiment with the steam options or WiFi.We're very pleased with this purchase. Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher because of the low noise, cost, and KitchenAid in November of 2022.
Comments (English): [ Beware. Run away as fast as you can ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher because of the low noise, cost, and KitchenAid in November of 2022. I have yet to be able to use it. When it arrived, one the the wheels on the middle rack was broken, so that rack is unable to be used. Upon installation and finding the problem, I immediately called KitchenAid. Having called the number before for problems with a warming drawer, I knew I was in for a frustrating time. So I listened to all their "advice" and commercials while waiting for a human. Fortunately, I was only handed off to a different department once. Finally I was able to describe the problem and get a wheel on order. Perhaps. There was some question of whether it was on backorder. So maybe it was ordered. Then, after hearing nothing for some time, I called back a few weeks later. The wheel had been sent. A FedEx tracking number was provided. However, the shipment had been stalled somewhere for a prolonged time. I called FedEx. The package had been damaged. It could not be delivered. I had to again call KitchenAid. Another wheel was sent. This was a month ago. I called back today, and was given a tracking number. The package has not moved in 3 weeks. They say it is lost and KitchenAid had to initiate a trace. This is for a plastic wheel about 3/4 inch in diameter. So, yet again, I called KitchenAid, mostly to listen to their prolonged inane messages at the beginning, because I so enjoy pointless delays. This time, when I finally got a human on the phone, he was unable to help and after being transferred to 2 other departments without anyone's meaningful assistance, I hung up in frustration. As much as I enjoy being on hold and listening to useless drivel, I decided to buy a wheel through a third party vendor. Even though a 50 cent piece is going to end up costing me 25 dollars, it might preserve my sanity today. While I agree that half of my frustration is toward the gorillas at FedEx, the amount of time I have spent on the phone with KitchenAid to get this one little wheel would fill up a large percentage of a workday. I was going to finish my kitchen with a KitchenAid refrigerator, having already purchased a double wall oven. However, given my experience with the warming drawer and now this dishwasher, I will go with Subzero instead. And if someone at KitchenAid does read this, please do not invite me to go to Facebook, twitter, or any other type of social media. I do not use any of those. Email me. The address is provided with this review. Please do not ask me to email you to restate the problem that I have just delineated. If you really want to help, I just need Part number W11545296. You can look up order number *** and get my contact info and address. Or email me and I will provide it.

Sentence (English): I ordered this dishwasher because many have recommended Bosch to me, as it should be an excellent long-lasting brand.
Comments (English): [ Unpleasant surprises ] || ---------------- || I ordered this dishwasher because many have recommended Bosch to me, as it should be an excellent long-lasting brand. Looking through the various dishwashers, this seemed to me to be at the right price and aesthetically beautiful. It's a pity that when it arrived home we realized that the white panel in front wasn't there, as you could guess from the photos. It wasn't even specified that you had to put your own panel, and furthermore I don't even have one to put in front of it since the previous dishwasher didn't require it. We also noticed the (non) quality of Bosch materials, in fact there are many plastic components even on the points of greatest stress (such as the doors and the lock) which will break in the long run.
Comments (Original): [ Spiacevoli sorprese ] || ---------------- || Ho ordinato questa lavastoviglie perché in molti mi hanno consigliato la Bosch, in quanto dovrebbe essere un'ottima marca duratura nel tempo. Cercando tra le varie lavastoviglie questa mi è sembrata al giusto prezzo e bella esteticamente. Peccato che quando è arrivata a casa ci siamo accorti che il pannello bianco davanti non c'era, come invece si intuiva dalle foto. Non era neanche specificato che bisognasse mettere il proprio pannello, e inoltre io non ne ho neanche uno da metterci davanti siccome la lavastoviglie precedente non lo richiedeva. Inoltre ci siamo accorti della (non) qualità dei materiali Bosch, infatti sono presenti tantissimi componenti in plastica anche sui punti di maggiore stress (come le ante e la serratura) che a lungo andare si spezzeranno.

Sentence (English): The Bosch Ascenta SHE3AR76UC is a fine dishwasher for its price.
Comments (English): [ Fine product; wish Bosch made other black models ] || ---------------- || The Bosch Ascenta SHE3AR76UC is a fine dishwasher for its price. However, if I could have bought a quieter model in black, I would have considered it. Our previous dishwasher was a 10-year-old 39-decibal Kenmore; this one is 50 db, and with our Great Room design, I would have preferred quieter. This one isn't loud. It's just louder than the whisper quiet machine it replaced - like the difference between a whisper and a low-volume voiced conversation. Beyond that, while I would have preferred all-stainless model, I like the price of this hybrid model. (This Ascenta is a hybrid with stainless sides and top with a plastic bottom.) I suspect this won't make much difference in washing ability, but the hybrid technology hasn't yet borne the test of time, and I still have some reservations about Bosch's choice to marry plastic to stainless steel on this Ascenta and its siblings. Beyond those concerns, this basic Bosch is great for our needs. It gets dishes clean, and it has all the features we need - a nine-hour delay start, an automatic setting, heavy wash, normal wash, delicate wash, express wash (one hour), half load, sanitize, and a button lock. (You have to read the manual to know how to active the button lock, but it's there.) Bosch customer service didn't seem to know whether this model uses the same brushless motor as the higher end models, but I'm hoping Bosch has used a motor commensurate with the company's fine reputation. This model doesn't dry plastic items as well as I'd like, but I'm willing to dry a few dishes to buy Bosch quality at half the price of a model that dries plastics well. Incidentally, the heat pump design on all Bosch dishwashers, this one included, (i.e. lack of a heating element at the base of the tub; the heat pump gets the water hot enough to remove grit and grime) allows us to place any item on the bottom rack. It's possible that some new dishwashers with a heating element might dry plastics better than our new Bosch, but our Kenmore with a heating element dried about the same as this one. For those on a budget or for those who desire black or white, this basic Bosch will get the job done.

Comments (English): [ Missing Feature ] || ---------------- || I debated on giving a 3- or 4-star rating. I have always liked/preferred Whirlpool appliances and know from experience they're top of the line in quality and performance. But I am so disappointed in Whirlpool for one particular total miss in one functionality of this dishwasher. One of the key features that led me to buy this model was the Quick Wash cycle. I live alone and thought this option would be ideal for my normally small loads. And while the cleaning capability using QW is fine, I was totally shocked to learn the same cannot be said about this cycle's drying ability. I quickly learned you cannot use extended dry with this cycle after several attempts proved the regular drying option leaves the dishes wet. They're about 2/3 to 3/4 dry and no matter how long you leave the door shut after the drying cycle ends most all of the dishes particularly in the 2nd or 3rd rack still remain wet enough they have to be manually or aired dry before putting away. I just don't understand why Whirlpool made the Extended Dry option unavailable with Quick Wash when the regular drying cycle misses the mark in drying capability. But not by much. So why couldn't they have bumped up the programmed regular drying time for QW just a tad? Bad miss, Whirlpool! IMHO, no dishwasher manufacturer should add a cycle on any model if it's not going to have both adequate washing AND drying functionality. Why would anyone want to use a dishwasher wash cycle and then have to dry dishes themselves? Rather defeats the purpose □□‍♀️

Sentence (English): I just love this dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Superb cleaning - steaming through the dishes ] || ---------------- || I just love this dishwasher! With the smart stainless steel finish and digital touch controls it will look great in any setting. It was simple to install with the hoses fitted, all ready to just connect to the water and waste pipes. There are numerous cycles and combinations of options to choose from according to your need at the time. I was attracted by the steam option which is everything I hoped for, getting the dishes sparkling clean, and when used with the intensive cycle handling the pots and baked on residue with ease. The auto cycle calculates itself how long to run based on how soiled the load is, and there is a turbo cycle which I also find useful for a faster finish, and an eco cycle for energy saving.The four way spray arms make sure the load is cleaned from every angle and right into the corners too. Connecting to WiFi means you are able to access smart options via the LG ThinQ app which can be connected to a phone to monitor efficiency, set alerts and help self diagnose should you hit a problem. Loading capacity is great and I can fit my big pans in without having to do a separate load which is far more efficient, saving time and cost. The dishwasher does come with noise strips to fit, however I have found it is super quiet to run even without them fitted. This is a great looking machine that gives excellent cleaning results. The steam option is definitely a worthwhile addition and I am very pleased with this purchase.

Comments (English): [ LG dishwasher takes washing to 21st century. ] || ---------------- || Have taken this new LG TrueSteam™ QuadWash™ Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel DB425TXS to replace a 12 year old machine from another known brand that always worked perfectly well.Like most people we tend to mostly use only two programmes The Eco programme - it saves water and energy and it takes just over 3 hours, so we run it overnight, but everything is sparkling clean and dry unless you have very dirty plates/pots in which case I suggest one of the other ones, personally my favourite is the Intensive as it manages to clear also the most dirty casserole dishes.Being used to the cutlery caddy I found using the cutlery drawer strange at first but it just took some time to get used to and it was absolutely fine after a while and washed well.Our old machine used to display a light on the floor to show it was on but this one shows you the amount of time the programme has to run, a nifty feature which also complements the ability to show the time left on the LG app.The LG ThinQ app was simple to download and set-up, having another LG smart appliance I was used to it, unfortunately setting up the dishwasher was a challenge and proved impossible using the auto settings therefore I had to resort to the manual installation which fortunately worked immediately.I find the app functions useful, but not life changing and probably not worth the “premium” price tag, still it is a nice added feature, same for the steam option which works well but have not noticed a major difference from the normal cycles, so overall I am very pleased with my purchase as another positive note is how quiet the machine is and I sometimes have to check the app to make sure it is actually on! I think another most useful feature is the automatic opening function at the end of each cycle which helps to make sure everything inside is sufficiently dry to not need a manual intervention before going back in the cupboard, especially if run overnight.A side note to LG customer service. I was extremely let down that, although I was offered free delivery and installation on this model, when the delivery company showed up as planned, they quite rudely informed me that because it was an integrated model, they would not install it (or even take it out of the box) and take away my old dishwasher. At this point LG customer service was useless and told me I had to arrange for my own installation and they could only ask again for the old dishwasher to be collected.

Sentence (English): I do love this machine.
Comments (English): [ Appreciation for "Mister Bosch" ] || ---------------- || I do love this machine. Surprised actually, but it lives up to the positive ratings on Consumer Reports and the NY Times. It delivers sparkling clean dry dishes, as long as you keep the drying agent filled. I do think the filling process for the drying agent could be easier. I transfer the drying agent to a smaller bottle so I can pour it in without hitting the vent. (Including a small plastic bottle with a long screw on nipple would make the task easier.) The third rack is a little fiddly and can get in the way of stem ware on the second level. But unloading the silverware from the machine directly to my silverware drawer is now actually fun. Thanks for that. I was intimidated by the 47 page instruction booklet at first but I now appreciate it because it shows that Bosch really takes its customer service seriously. Kind of a rare quality in todays world. Also, as long as I leave some bit of space between dishes, I can load a lot of dishes in and still get very clean dishes. Must be the multiple spray arms. Thanks for that too. In general, I am really enjoying using this machine. It is a welcome assistant in my kitchen. We are calling our machine "Mister Bosch" because it deserves respect.

Surprised actually, but it lives up to the positive ratings on Consumer Reports and the NY Times. It delivers sparkling clean dry dishes, as long as you keep the drying agent filled. I do think the filling process for the drying agent could be easier. I transfer the drying agent to a smaller bottle so I can pour it in without hitting the vent. (Including a small plastic bottle with a long screw on nipple would make the task easier.) The third rack is a little fiddly and can get in the way of stem ware on the second level. But unloading the silverware from the machine directly to my silverware drawer is now actually fun. Thanks for that. I was intimidated by the 47 page instruction booklet at first but I now appreciate it because it shows that Bosch really takes its customer service seriously. Kind of a rare quality in todays world. Also, as long as I leave some bit of space between dishes, I can load a lot of dishes in and still get very clean dishes. Must be the multiple spray arms. Thanks for that too. In general, I am really enjoying using this machine. It is a welcome assistant in my kitchen. We are calling our machine "Mister Bosch" because it deserves respect.

Sentence (English): I have had this dishwasher nearly 2 months now.
Comments (English): [ Excellent clean & dry, still figuring out layout ] || ---------------- || I have had this dishwasher nearly 2 months now. It replaced another brand's less experience model. I went through an appliance specialist in my area and after the 3rd repair call (under warranty on the other brand), they gave me a store credit. I decided to upgrade in looks and features. Overall, I am pleased with the purchase, but it could be better. Pros: the look. It looks extremely refined and the stainless steel is smudge proof. This is great in a small kitchen with pets. I can take or leave the handle, but don't run into it like I was worried about. I love the door controls. These are rarely set off accidentally. I also love that after you choose a setting it counts down for the door to close before beginning the cycle. I have only tried a few of the cycle options, but everything comes out better than expected. I typically use the "normal" setting with pro dry or express wash with pro dry. I am impressed at how clean the dishes, utensils, and Tupperware get. I am more impressed at how dry everything gets. Size- due to large tub size I've had to run this 1/3 the amount I used to. This may also be due to the 3rd rack. The stainless steel tub seems more hygenic and easy to clean. Cons: Cycle times. This isn't a huge thing for my household because there are only 2 humans (there are 4 legged housemates that have their own dishes), but we don't have to run it often. The racks! I am not sure if I'm still figuring it out, but the racks are setup super weird. It is advertised as adjustable and having all of these great features, but there isn't even a place for a 13x9 pan on the bottom. No matter where you put it, it either doesn't fit or topples over. I don't really want my glaxx pyrex dishes flailing around every time I open the dishwasher. The changeable/adjustable racks on the 2nd/3rd racks don't help fit bowls or plates and I feel like there is a lot of wasted space. We can get by because we are a small household, but I would be peeved if we had a large family. I could definitely fit more in my old dishwasher based on space optimization.

Sentence (English): When you go 21 years with a functioning appliance and then decide to upgrade, it's like going to another planet.
Comments (English): [ Replacing an older dishwasher ] || ---------------- || When you go 21 years with a functioning appliance and then decide to upgrade, it's like going to another planet.There are a whole bunch of design and function improvements that passed me by in the past two decades.First, I'm most impressed with the sound insulation. With the machine running, you could listen to a violin concerto at low volume and never miss a note. It's impressively quiet.Second, the tall tub configuration means a lot more dish and pan volume. I haven't been at risk for running out of room, yet. And the adjustable racks are really helpful when washing tall pans and grill parts.That narrow 3rd pull out shelf on the top is a big plus for things like tongs, spatulas and tools. Probably most importantly, the machine cleans very well, and at the 'normal' dry setting, does an excellent job of delivering dry dishes and mostly dry utensils. I have yet to use the bottle jets which require a special cycle setting, so I cannot comment on that feature.I'm a very happy consumer.

Sentence (English): I bought a dishwasher for my newlyweds.
Comments (English): [ I bought a dishwasher for my honeymoon. I was looking for a Samsung sale event. ] || ---------------- || I bought a dishwasher for my newlyweds. I was looking for it, and there was a Samsung sale event, so I bought it from Samsung.com. I'm so proud that I bought it at a good price. The installer also kindly explained it well and installed it well. It's the first time I've used it, and I'm so glad it worked out well. But I don't know if it's a built-in free standing combination. I thought it was a built-in product, but later I found out that it was a combined product; . The top plate is said to be stored separately. I am satisfied with the cleaning power. I just have to install induction again . I'm a little worried that steam coming out of the dishwasher might cause problems with the induction. What as is going well, is it okay?
Comments (Original): [ 신혼살림으로 식세기를 구매하였습니다.찾아보다가 삼성 세일 이벤... ] || ---------------- || 신혼살림으로 식세기를 구매하였습니다.찾아보다가 삼성 세일 이벤트가 있어서 삼성닷컴에서 구매하였고요.좋은 가격에 산듯해서 너무 뿌듯합니다.설치기사님도 친절하게 잘 설명해주시고 잘 설치해주시고 가셨습니다.처음 써봣는데 깨긋하게 잘되서 너무 좋네요.근데 빌트인 프리스탠딩 겸용인지 모르고 삿네요.빌트인제품인지 알았는데 나중에 보니 겸용이더군요;;;상판은 따로 보관해야한다고하네요ㅠ세척력이 좋아서 만족스럽습니다.다만 인덕션을 또 설치해야되는데식세기에서 나오는 수증기 같은게 인덕션에 문제를 일으키지는 않을까 조금 걱정됩니다.뭐 as잘되니 괜찮겟죠?

The pots and bowls of a family of three with double-layer bowls and baskets can be saved and washed once a day. The fly in the ointment is that I still like the panel with physical button operation, and I don't feel comfortable with touch operation.

Sentence (English): Pretty much the only portable dishwasher left on the market.
Comments (English): [ Have had better, much better. ] || ---------------- || Pretty much the only portable dishwasher left on the market. I have a very old house and it does not have a place for an under the counter dishwasher. This is the 3rd one I have had to purchase since 2014, so I guess 5 years for a machine isn't all that bad no a days? But this one is HORRIBLE! So very noisy and the wheels don't lock, so the thing will move all over if you don't secure it somehow. We have it plumbed into place so we don't need it to move around, but it wants to! The racks have the weirdest spacing on them ever! No place for serving bowls or really anything that isn't a flat dinner or salad plate. The prongs are spaced about 1"-1&1/2" apart. So it's a very tricky job to load anything except flat dishes. The worst thing is that it will NOT dry the dishes unless you IMMEDIATELY crack open the door! And this is exactly how it is written in the manual. Who wants to wait up for the cycle to be finished to have to run to it and open the door a crack? I will definitely be looking for another one once this $700+ thing is paid off!

Sentence (English): Had to replace a relatively new Bosch dishwasher that was damaged by an electrical surge when a drunk driver knocked down the pole outside my house.
Comments (English): [ Really pleased with this unit so far! ] || ---------------- || Had to replace a relatively new Bosch dishwasher that was damaged by an electrical surge when a drunk driver knocked down the pole outside my house. Repairing the Bosch would take significant time (weeks) to get parts ordered/installed and there was a good chance I'd spend the price of a new unit doing the repairs. As there were no Bosch units even for sale at my usual retailers and I've had excellent results with LG appliances (two stoves), I gave this one a shot. I am not disappointed. It's as quiet as the Bosch, has a better user interface (Bosch's is clunky to me) and has some cool features (the downloadable wash mode is genius if you ask me) including Alexa and other home automation integration. Honestly, for less money than I paid for the Bosch I feel like I got a better dishwasher. I didn't do the Costco install (too many complaints in reviews and having a separate appt to wait for made no sense). And I've installed many dishwashers so it was no issue. The unit was well packed in the carton and no damage. Delivery guys hauled out my already-disconnected Bosch, dropped off the LG and went on their way. It probably would have been better if they unpacked it but I think they normally don't with an installed item. The cardboard bottom of the carton was soaked and falling apart but the dishwasher is sitting on a thick foam cushion so it was perfectly dry. Seems like the box must have sat in water for a long time to get that bad though. Install was easy (again, I've done it before). Electrical, water input and the drain hose were in basically the same locations as the Bosch and they have convenient channels to run the lines under the unit without crushing them. It was easy to level the unit both front and back. The front feet are snug to get moving at first so a wrench on the top is far easier than using a screwdriver to turn the feet. Once loosened you can tilt the unit up a bit and turn them by hand if you like. There's also a screw in front that raises and lowers the back to simplify leveling the rear of the unit. I got the water inlet connected (no leaks) and wrestled the drain hose onto my disposal inlet (the connection is tight to get on but so far it's holding well with the clamp provided). Once the breaker was flipped on, the unit fired right up. Ran a test run and it ran quietly and completely with no leaks or errors. I did notice some water on the floor after a full run but I'm pretty sure it is dripping from the door when it is opened. Still need to look at that but I'm pretty sure it's not the water inlet, drain or seal around the door. Over the last few days I've run it several times and I'm very pleased with the cleaning results. I don't kill myself to wash off plates too much but I also don't burn on a lot of stuff that's tough to remove. Everything is coming out clean and clear so no complaints on that. The features, price and quality of this unit make it a bargain if you ask me. And if you can do the install yourself, do it. It's not very hard.

Sentence (English): When you go 21 years with a functioning appliance and then decide to upgrade, it's like going to another planet.
Comments (English): [ Replacing an older dishwasher ] || ---------------- || When you go 21 years with a functioning appliance and then decide to upgrade, it's like going to another planet. There are a whole bunch of design and function improvements that passed me by in the past two decades. First, I'm most impressed with the sound insulation. With the machine running, you could listen to a violin concerto at low volume and never miss a note. It's impressively quiet. Second, the tall tub configuration means a lot more dish and pan volume. I haven't been at risk for running out of room, yet. And the adjustable racks are really helpful when washing tall pans and grill parts. That narrow 3rd pull out shelf on the top is a big plus for things like tongs, spatulas and tools. Probably most importantly, the machine cleans very well, and at the 'normal' dry setting, does an excellent job of delivering dry dishes and mostly dry utensils. I have yet to use the bottle jets which require a special cycle setting, so I cannot comment on that feature. I'm a very happy consumer.

Sentence (English): We had a Bosch dishwasher and replaced it with this GE dishwasher when we remodeled the kitchen (we replaced all our appliances with the GE Profile series).
Comments (English): [ Prefer our old dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We had a Bosch dishwasher and replaced it with this GE dishwasher when we remodeled the kitchen (we replaced all our appliances with the GE Profile series). I do not like the exposed drying/heating elements in the bottom of the dishwasher. Many of our taller glasses, pans, and utensils do not fit in this unit without adjusting the height down, which then results in the spinning water arms from turning because they hit the plates or other things. We used to fill the Bosch over a period of a few days, but with the GE unit, we end up running it almost every day with fewer items so we don't have issues with the water arms hitting dishes. We've also noticed that the dishwasher pods do not always dissolve, which results in a paste inside the pod dispenser.Our glasses are becoming very cloudy very fast with this dishwasher, too. There are many features that might be ok, but we don't really use any of them.One of the things I do like about this dishwasher is the ability to connect via wi-fi to get an alert when it finishes (this was an add-on module). It is better with fingerprints and smudges than our old dishwasher.

Sentence (English): We had a limited budget for the entire kitchen and that's why it went with the Series 4 dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Exceeded my expectations ] || ---------------- || We had a limited budget for the entire kitchen and that's why it went with the Series 4 dishwasher. We didn't really think about it much before buying it. Now I'm very excited about the device. It can be operated smartly and has therefore received additional programs. The device is very quiet and cleans the dishes well. The additional drying function works great and allows the tupperware to dry well. The device reports via the home connect app when the rinse aid or salt needs to be refilled. What I don't like so much is that it is displayed in the Bosch smart home system but not operated. If you press the dishwasher tile you will only be redirected to the home connect app. I would like to see Bosch grow more together across all business areas there. But since I didn't expect the smart function at all, I am completely satisfied with the device.
Comments (Original): [ Hat meine Erwartungen übertroffen ] || ---------------- || Wir hatten ein begrenztes Budget für die gesamte Küche und deshalb ist es der Geschirrspüler der Serie 4 geworden. Wir haben uns auch gar nicht groß damit beschäftigt vor dem Kauf. Nun bin ich doch sehr begeistert vom Gerät. Es lässt sich smart bedienen und hat dadurch zusätzliche Programme erhalten. Das Gerät ist sehr leise und macht das Geschirr gut sauber. Die zusätzliche Trocknungsfunktion funktioniert super und lässt die tupperware gut trocknen. Das Gerät meldet über die home connect App wenn der Klarspüler oder das Salz nachgefüllt werden muss. Was mir nicht so gut gefällt ist, dass es im Bosch smart home System zwar angezeigt wird aber nicht bedient. Wenn man auf die Kachel des Geschirrspüler drückt wird man lediglich zur home connect App weitergeleitet. Ich wünsche mir dass bosch dort Geschäftsfeld übergreifend mehr zusammenwächst. Aber da ich die smarte Funktion gar nicht erwartet hatte, bin ich vollsten zufrieden mit dem Gerät.

Sentence (English): I ordered this unit after contemplating purchasing one of those newer counter-top models which looked kinda cool but rather insubstantial for the often grimy job of cleaning dirty dishes and flatware!
Comments (English): [ Perfect for a small kitchen ] || ---------------- || I ordered this unit after contemplating purchasing one of those newer counter-top models which looked kinda cool but rather insubstantial for the often grimy job of cleaning dirty dishes and flatware! This GE slim unit looks well made and seems solid enuf after several months of light but regular use. It also has a stainless steel interior as well. (Btw, after experimenting w/ different kinds of liquid dishwasher detergents I finally settled on using the premesured pods which I simply toss in the bottom just prior to using. The dishes come out spotless and squeaky clean every time.). I also use the shortest and most basic clean and rinse cycle as well, and the dishes as I said are as clean as I ever have seen any dishes! Another quick note, I also no longer rinse the dishes before placing them in the rack. I do scrape any large remaining scraps of food, gravy, crumbs etc. but leave the remaining residue for the washer as this coating actually allows the dish detergents to adhere to the surface of the dish even better than if they had been rinsed prior to running a wash cycle. This both saves water and time but also increases the effectiveness of the washing machine process as well. Anyway, it's also a doubly useful item in my very compact little log-cabin kitchen, because w/ the addition of a large cutting board on top it's now also a movable food prep island as well. I decided on getting a dishwasher in the first place because despite not really minding do the dishes by hand I just never felt that with the maximum amount of hot water even my rubber-gloved hands could tolerate it was still not sufficiently hot enuf to sterilize the dirty dishes well enuf for my liking! So yes this is a ringing endorsement, so far with absolutely no downsides that I can as yet identify! If you have a small kitchen like mine where a built-in dishwasher is simply impractical and unwanted yet like me you want the through dish cleaning and sterilization that only happens with very hot water, then this is a very good choice in my opinion!

Sentence (English): This unit comes with a power plug configured for a European outlet.
Comments (English): [ Installers Beware ] || ---------------- || This unit comes with a power plug configured for a European outlet. Therefore, you are required to purchase (sold separately) a junction box with an attached power cord. Installation requires routing the existing power supply to an adjacent cabinet, installing junction box and rerouting supply cord back into dishwasher cabinet. Installing junction box in an already space challenged adjacent cabinet can be problematic. In addition, if your electric supply is located in a cabinet to the left of the dishwasher, the length of the supply cord from the junction box to the insert point at the back of the unit (right rear) could be an issue. I've installed several Bosch dishwashers in the past, all of which had the power connection terminal in the lower front (right) of the unit. This model/series was configured for a European outlet supply.

Sentence (English): An extremely speechless shopping experience.
Comments (English): An extremely speechless shopping experience. The machine I bought cost 1,100 yuan to complete the cabinet renovation. After the machine was installed, two alarm failures occurred. When I contacted customer service, I was asked to find insurance at first, and then asked me to find after-sales service. I saw that it was a machine problem and asked me to apply for a refund online. The online refund application was rejected. I called the after-sales service and said that the machine would be taken away offline. To make a refund, you have to wait for their approval. The whole process is like a joke. I have to say that the offline after-sales service and attitude are really good, but what I question is Haier's after-sales process? that's all? I am also speechless for such a big company. Let’s talk about the machine, it’s full of cheap feeling, the panel feels like a layer of iron, and the plastic smell inside is particularly strong when you open it. I think it’s enough to wash 12 sets of bowls. After all, the width is here, and now the hole in the cabinet is dug there. What to do, anyway, I feel that most of the good reviews should be the reason for the 100 yuan cash back.
Comments (Original): 极其无语的一次购物经历，买到的机器自己花了1100块钱完成橱柜改造，装好后机器出现两项报警故障，找客服，一开始说让我找保险，后来让我找售后，售后上门看过确认是机器问题让我线上申请退款，线上申请退款被拒绝，打电话给售后，说线下把机器拉走，然后私人***信，说过两天微信给**作退款，具体要等他们审批好，全程都像在搞笑一样，不得不说线下售后的服务以及态度确实不错，但我质疑的这就是海尔的售后流程？就这样吗？这么大一公司，我也是无语。再说机器吧，满满的廉价感，面板感觉就是一层铁皮，打开里面塑料味特别大，我觉得洗12套碗够呛，毕竟宽度在这里，现在橱柜的坑挖在那里了，也不知道该怎么办了，反正我感觉这好评应该大多是100块钱的现金返还的原因吧。

Sentence (English): I got this LG dishwasher after my previous (mostly dependable) Kitchen-Aid washer quit.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and Intuitive ] || ---------------- || I got this LG dishwasher after my previous (mostly dependable) Kitchen-Aid washer quit. I was worried the LG would be louder but just the opposite; turns out to be quieter. The controls are simple to use and, unlike the Kitchen-Aid, can't be activated by leaning against them, something that happened often. The lay-out of the controls is intuitive so much so I didn't even need the instructions to figure it out. And by the way, I really appreciated the one page quick-look instruction sheet. I always disliked having to read through a manual. The only thing I'd change is the dishwasher is white but the bottom kick-panel is black and the installation instructions say not to cover up the kick-panel with a trim-panel. Since my trim panels are white like the dishwasher, the black stands out. I'll probably take it off and spray paint it white. Overall, I like it lots and highly recommend it.
